# STE-C dictionary

The code rules use these words. A project adds its own words in LEXICON.md.

## Approved verbs

Each verb has one contract. Use it only for that contract.

| Verb | Meaning | Do not use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `get` | Return a value that is already in memory. No I/O. | network (fetch), storage (load), slow work (compute) |
| `set` | Replace one value in memory. | a change to a stored entity (update) |
| `find` | Search for one item. Return nothing when there is no match. | a search that must succeed (get) |
| `list` | Return all items that match, as a collection. The collection can be empty. | one item (find) |
| `count` | Return the number of items. | the items themselves (list) |
| `fetch` | Get a value from a remote system over the network. | local storage (load) |
| `load` | Read a stored value from a disk, a database, or a cache into memory. | network calls (fetch) |
| `save` | Write a value to persistent storage. Create it or replace it. | a stream (write) |
| `read` | Read bytes, lines, or records from a stream or a file. | a parsed value (parse or load) |
| `write` | Write bytes, lines, or records to a stream or a file. | a stored entity (save) |
| `create` | Make a new persistent entity and give it an identity. Fail if it exists. | a value in memory only (build) |
| `build` | Construct a value in memory from its parts. No I/O. | a persistent entity (create) |
| `update` | Change some fields of an existing entity. Fail if it does not exist. | a value in memory (set) |
| `delete` | Remove an entity from storage permanently. | an item in a collection (remove) |
| `add` | Put an item into a collection. | a new persistent entity (create) |
| `remove` | Take an item out of a collection. The item can still exist in other places. | permanent removal from storage (delete) |
| `insert` | Put an item into a collection at a given position. | a collection with no order (add) |
| `append` | Put an item at the end of a sequence. | a collection with no order (add) |
| `clear` | Remove all items from a collection. | a full object state (reset) |
| `reset` | Put an object back into its initial state. | a collection only (clear) |
| `replace` | Put a new value in the place of an old value. | a partial change (update) |
| `rename` | Give an existing item a new name. | a move to a different location (move) |
| `move` | Put an existing item in a different location. | a duplicate (copy) |
| `copy` | Make an independent duplicate. | a shared reference (get) |
| `parse` | Convert text or bytes into a structured value. Fail on bad input. | output for people (format) |
| `format` | Convert a structured value into text for people. | a wire format (encode) |
| `encode` | Convert a value into a wire format or a storage format. | text for people (format) |
| `decode` | Convert a wire format or a storage format into a value. | free text (parse) |
| `to` | Convert a value to a different type. No side effects. | a conversion that can fail (parse) |
| `normalize` | Convert a value into its one canonical form. | a check (validate) |
| `escape` | Replace special characters so that a different language reads the text literally. | a removal of characters (strip) |
| `strip` | Remove characters or markup from text. | a removal of a collection item (remove) |
| `split` | Divide one value into a sequence of parts. | a filter of items (filter) |
| `join` | Combine a sequence of parts into one value. | a combination of two records (merge) |
| `merge` | Combine two or more records into one record. | a sequence of text parts (join) |
| `sort` | Put items in order. | a removal of items (filter) |
| `filter` | Keep only the items that match a condition. | one item (find) |
| `map` | Apply one function to each item and return the results. | side effects only (apply) |
| `compare` | Return the order of two values or the difference between them. | a pass or fail result (validate) |
| `match` | Test a value against a pattern. Return the match or nothing. | a rule set (validate) |
| `compute` | Derive a value from inputs. No side effects. It can be slow. | a value in memory (get) |
| `measure` | Record the size, the duration, or the rate of an operation. | a count of items (count) |
| `validate` | Test a value against rules. Return the result or the list of errors. Do not throw for bad input. | a guard that throws (assert) |
| `assert` | Test a condition. Throw or panic when it is false. | a test that returns a result (validate) |
| `ensure` | Make a condition true. Do nothing when it is already true. | a test only (validate) |
| `resolve` | Find the final value of a reference, such as a path, a host name, or a promise. | a search in a collection (find) |
| `send` | Transmit a message to one known receiver. | an event for many listeners (emit) |
| `emit` | Publish an event to zero or more listeners. Do not wait for them. | one known receiver (send) |
| `subscribe` | Register a listener for an event. | a registry entry (register) |
| `unsubscribe` | Remove a listener for an event. | a registry entry (unregister) |
| `register` | Add an item to a registry so that other code can find it. | an event listener (subscribe) |
| `unregister` | Remove an item from a registry. | an event listener (unsubscribe) |
| `start` | Begin a process, a service, or a timer that runs for a long time. | a job that runs to completion (run) |
| `stop` | End a process, a service, or a timer. | an operation that did not begin (cancel) |
| `run` | Execute a job, a command, or a task to completion. | a long-running service (start) |
| `cancel` | Stop a pending operation before it completes. | a running service (stop) |
| `schedule` | Arrange an operation to run at a later time. | an operation that runs now (run) |
| `wait` | Block until a condition is true or a timeout ends. | a later operation (schedule) |
| `retry` | Run an operation again after it fails. | the first attempt (run) |
| `open` | Acquire a resource handle, such as a file or a connection. | a network session (connect) |
| `close` | Release a resource handle. | a network session (disconnect) |
| `connect` | Start a session with a remote system. | a local file (open) |
| `disconnect` | End a session with a remote system. | a local file (close) |
| `lock` | Get exclusive access to a resource. | a permission change (disable) |
| `unlock` | Release exclusive access to a resource. | a permission change (enable) |
| `enable` | Turn on a feature or a setting. | a service (start) |
| `disable` | Turn off a feature or a setting. | a service (stop) |
| `apply` | Put a change, a patch, or a configuration into effect on a target. | a conversion (map) |
| `render` | Produce output for display, such as a page, a view, or a template. | text for a log (format) |
| `show` | Make a user interface element visible. | output to a stream (write) |
| `hide` | Make a user interface element invisible. | a removal (remove) |
| `log` | Write one event to the log. | output for the user (write) |
| `import` | Bring external records into the system. | a stored value (load) |
| `export` | Send records out of the system in an external format. | a stored value (save) |
| `upload` | Send a file to a remote system. | a message (send) |
| `download` | Get a file from a remote system. | a structured value (fetch) |
| `install` | Put a package, a hook, or a component in place so that it can run. | a registry entry (register) |
| `uninstall` | Remove an installed package, hook, or component. | a stored entity (delete) |
| `push` | Put an item on the top of a stack or the end of a queue. | a collection with no order (add) |
| `pop` | Take the item from the top of a stack or the front of a queue. | a collection with no order (remove) |
| `wrap` | Put a value inside a different value that adds context. | a type conversion (to) |
| `accept` | Take an incoming request, a connection, or an offer. | a check (validate) |
| `reject` | Refuse an incoming request, a connection, or an offer. | a removal (remove) |
| `test` | Make sure that code obeys its contract. Use it only in test code. | production checks (validate) |

## Predicates and prefixes

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `is` | The value is in a state or belongs to a kind. |
| `has` | The value owns or contains an item. |
| `can` | The actor has the permission or the capability. |
| `should` | A policy decides that the action is correct. |
| `on` | An event callback. The rest of the name is the event. Example: `onOrderCanceled`. |
| `try` | Return a result or nothing instead of an exception. The next word is an approved verb. Example: `tryParseDate`. |

## Verbs to avoid

| Do not use | Use |
|---|---|
| `handle` | the exact verb, or on<Event> for a callback |
| `process` | parse, validate, to, or compute |
| `manage` | the exact verb: create, update, delete, or schedule |
| `do` | the exact verb |
| `perform` | run, or the exact verb |
| `execute` | run |
| `retrieve` | get, fetch, or load |
| `obtain` | get, fetch, or load |
| `grab` | get, fetch, or load |
| `modify` | update or set |
| `change` | update or set |
| `edit` | update or set |
| `alter` | update or set |
| `destroy` | delete |
| `erase` | delete |
| `purge` | delete |
| `kill` | stop |
| `terminate` | stop |
| `halt` | stop |
| `make` | build or create |
| `calculate` | compute |
| `calc` | compute |
| `check` | validate, assert, or a predicate such as is or has |
| `verify` | validate or assert |
| `init` | start, create, or build |
| `initialize` | start, create, or build |
| `setup` | start, create, build, or install |
| `populate` | load or set |
| `fill` | load or set |

## Words to avoid in names

| Do not use | Use |
|---|---|
| `data` | the name of what it holds: rows, payload, invoice |
| `info` | the name of what it holds |
| `stuff` | the name of what it holds |
| `thing` | the name of what it is |
| `things` | the name of what they are |
| `obj` | the name of what it is |
| `val` | the name of what it is |
| `tmp` | the name of what it holds |
| `res` | response or result |
| `ret` | the name of what the function returns |
| `foo` | a real name |
| `baz` | a real name |
| `util` | the name of the domain: dates, paths, money |
| `utils` | the name of the domain: dates, paths, money |
| `helper` | the name of the domain or the role |
| `helpers` | the name of the domain or the role |
| `misc` | the name of the domain |
| `manager` | the name of the role: store, scheduler, registry, router |
| `handler` | the name of the role, or on<Event> for a callback |
| `processor` | the name of the role: parser, validator, converter |
| `impl` | the name of the variant |

## Abbreviations

These abbreviations are approved:

- `id`, `ids`, `url`, `urls`, `uri`, `http`, `https`, `api`
- `json`, `xml`, `html`, `css`, `sql`, `csv`, `pdf`, `db`
- `io`, `ui`, `os`, `cpu`, `gpu`, `ip`, `tcp`, `udp`
- `tls`, `dns`, `jwt`, `uuid`, `utc`, `max`, `min`, `config`
- `env`, `app`, `auth`, `admin`, `repo`, `ms`, `ns`, `ok`
- `args`, `ctx`, `err`, `src`, `dst`, `dir`, `stdin`, `stdout`
- `stderr`, `async`, `sync`, `regex`, `ast`, `cli`, `sdk`, `ttl`
- `pr`, `ci`, `md`

Do not use these abbreviations:

| Do not use | Use |
|---|---|
| `usr` | user |
| `pwd` | password |
| `passwd` | password |
| `msg` | message |
| `msgs` | messages |
| `btn` | button |
| `cnt` | count |
| `num` | number or count |
| `idx` | index |
| `arr` | the name of what the list holds |
| `cfg` | config |
| `conf` | config |
| `mgr` | the name of the role |
| `evt` | event |
| `cb` | callback, or on<Event> |
| `el` | element |
| `elem` | element |
| `attr` | attribute |
| `attrs` | attributes |
| `prev` | previous |
| `cur` | current |
| `curr` | current |
| `resp` | response |
| `req` | request |
| `len` | length |
| `str` | text, or the name of what it holds |
| `buf` | buffer |
| `addr` | address |
| `ctrl` | controller |
| `svc` | service |
| `srv` | server |
| `lst` | the name of what the list holds |
| `fn` | the name of the function role |
| `func` | the name of the function role |

## Synonym groups

In one codebase, use one verb from a group for one object (C1.3).

- `get`, `fetch`, `load`, `read`, `retrieve`, `obtain`, `grab`
- `create`, `build`, `make`, `generate`, `new`
- `delete`, `remove`, `destroy`, `erase`, `drop`, `purge`
- `update`, `set`, `modify`, `change`, `edit`, `alter`, `patch`
- `validate`, `assert`, `check`, `verify`
- `compute`, `calculate`, `calc`, `derive`
- `start`, `init`, `initialize`, `launch`, `begin`, `boot`
- `stop`, `kill`, `terminate`, `halt`, `end`
- `send`, `emit`, `publish`, `dispatch`, `post`
